description: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis: grown for its white curd.

diseases.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of cauliflower and other brassicas with dark, target-like spots.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on brassica debris and seed and spread by wind and rain in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Round brown to black spots with concentric rings
A yellow halo round the spots
Dark spots on heads and stems too
diseases.effect: Spotted outer leaves and blemished heads reduce quality.
diseases.untreated: Severe spotting reaches the harvested part.

steps.title: Remove spotted outer leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted outer leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Rotate away from brassicas for 3 years

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
Wind and rain carry spores to leaves.
Dark ringed spots with halos form.
Spots reach the heads in wet weather.

diseases.name: Bacterial Soft Rot
diseases.description: A bacterial rot that turns parts of the cauliflower curd soft, slimy and foul-smelling.
diseases.causes: Soil bacteria enter the curd through wounds, insect damage and frost cracks, especially when water sits on the head in warm weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked, tan patches on the curd
The patches turn soft, slimy and brown
diseases.effect: Rotted heads are lost, in the field and in storage.
diseases.untreated: The rot spreads to neighbouring heads in wet weather.

steps.title: Remove rotting heads
steps.instruction: Cut out and remove rotting heads at once.
steps.rationale: They ooze bacteria onto the soil and tools.

steps.title: Keep heads dry
steps.instruction: Water at the base and improve drainage.
steps.rationale: Water on the curd lets the bacteria in.

steps.title: Harvest with care
steps.instruction: Avoid bruising heads; cool them quickly.

lifecycle: Soil bacteria splash onto the plant.
They enter through wounds in the curd.
Water-soaked patches go soft and slimy.
Ooze spreads them to other heads.
